relevance_note: The paper describes seven members of one family (P1–P7) with a germline TNFAIP3 variant ("identified a heterozygous c.2209delC mutation that was present in all members tested") who "were all diagnosed with HA20."
method_note: Read the full Markdown text (no '## Supplementary material' section). Tables 1 and 2 appear in the converted file as captions only, with no data rows or cells: Table 1 ('Results of pre-treatment thyroid function tests and anti-thyroid autoantibodies') and Table 2 ('Results of HLA allele typing') therefore yielded no cells to transcribe, and no table contained ' / ' stacked values. No script was used; spans were checked by eye against the paper text. All seven people are one Japanese family labelled P1–P7; the paper states they 'were all diagnosed with HA20'. Variant fields: 'We, therefore, analyzed TNFAIP3 in the present family (P1–P7)' plus 'a heterozygous c.2209delC mutation that was present in all members tested' is treated as a named-group statement covering P1–P7 (zygosity heterozygous, transcript NM_006290.2); variant_type_as_stated is 'not reported' because the authors never name a class for this variant, and the type was not derived from the HGVS string. 'In vitro functional analysis of this variant was previously reported as a pathogenic mutation (2).' is taken as functional evidence and author pathogenicity for this same variant. Inheritance is 'not reported' for everyone: the paper never says whether either parent carries the variant and never describes parental testing, and P1's mother (P2) is affected but not stated to be variant-tested. Contradictions: the paper presents P1–P7 as patients with an autoinflammatory disease and then says P1, P6 and P7 'have normal thyroid functions and no anti-thyroid autoantibodies, but are too young for this to be apparent' — the hedge is kept in the spans and the same rows are used for the checklist. Ambiguous or hedged statements were not scored as features: P2's 'possible Crohn’s disease' and episodes 'suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease', P7's perineal fistula 'possibly associated with inflammatory bowel disease' (gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation left 'not reported' for both, though P2's colonoscopy finding is kept as a phenotypic feature with its 'possible' wording), and P4's malignant lymphoma (kept as a feature but not counted as lymphoproliferation, since lymphoma is not lymphadenopathy or lymphoproliferation as described). Discussion sentences about previously published people (the HLA-B27 patient of ref 2, the GD case of ref 2, the HA20 patient with HT of ref 15, the ALPS-like patient of ref 4) give no individual-level fact beyond the diagnosis and are out of scope: no rows. For P1, P6 and P7 the group sentence 'have normal thyroid functions and no anti-thyroid autoantibodies' is used to mark 'autoimmune thyroiditis' and 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' excluded, with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'; the same sentence names P1, P6 and P7 explicitly. No 'Hashimoto's thyroiditis' item exists in the checklist, so HT is carried in disease_label_as_stated and phenotypic_features and mapped to the checklist item 'autoimmune thyroiditis'. P2, P3, P4 and P5 'appeared to have an A*24:02-B*54:01-C*01:02-DRB1*14:03 haplotype' is recorded only as a phenotypic feature (HLA haplotype), not as a checklist item. Age at last evaluation: the ages given as 'currently 6-, 2-, and 1-yr-old' were used for P1, P6 and P7, and P4's antibody measurement age ('at 34 yr of age') was treated as his last evaluation. Sex, consanguinity, vital status and treatment (except P3's levothyroxine) are not reported; the pedigree figure could not be read, so family relationships were taken from the text only. Re-report: 'A brief case report mentioning this family was previously described by Kadowaki et al. as part of a study examining HA20 patients in nine independent Japanese families (2).'
